newsitem.title: USA: White House declines comment on Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: White House declines comment on Netanyahu.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry on Monday declined comment on a decision by Israeli prosecutors not to file charges against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a corruption scandal.
"We have said that that's a domestic matter and has to be addressed domestically," McCurry told reporters.

Israel's attorney-general, Elyakim Rubinstein, said on Sunday no charges would be filed against Netanyahu, citing insufficient evidence in the affair, which concerned his short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general in January.

"The decision is to close the file, because of lack of evidence, against the prime minister, the minister of justice and lawyer (Roni) Bar-On and weigh whether to bring an indictment against legislator (Aryeh) Deri," Attorney General Elyakim Rubinstein said at a news conference.

Rubinstein said Deri could eventually be charged with fraud, breach of trust and extortion in connection with the brief appointment of Bar-On, an activist in Netanyahu's Likud party, as attorney-general.

An Israel Television report at the time alleged that Deri, already embroiled in a corruption trial, had coerced the Likud-led government to appoint Bar-On, who would then offer him a plea bargain. Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid a public outcry he was a legal lightweight unqualified for the job.
Police had recommended charges against Netanyahu, Deri, Justice Minister Tzachi Hanegbi and Avidgor Lieberman, director-general of the prime minister's office.

But Rubinstein told the news conference that the police case against Netanyahu was based on testimony of one witness which he said was insufficient for bringing charges. He said prosecutors had yet to decide whether to indict Lieberman.
